items.title: 66100_Bud Freeman oral history interview
items.q: Max was my saxophone teacher -- I studied many times with different people and he was a beautiful musician

ctx.x: Bud, one thing I think that should be said in fairness to Benny and I'll see if you agree with me, and that is the way he was endowed made it hard on Benny because it came naturally, he studied hard and worked hard, but the gift was there and in all fairness to Benny, he never -- I don't think that Benny really recognized the size of his gift, he thought that this is what is meant by saying you're a musician, and he judged people by what he had. He wondered why people -- he wondered why guys were slow.

I will tell you something analogous to that, very interesting. There was a great, to me, the best saxophone player I ever heard, not jazz, but a great musician by the name of Max Farley. You wouldn't have known about him because he goes way back to the early Whiteman days and Whiteman used to say about him, I never saw him sober but I never heard him make a mistake.
There was a marvelous thing. Max was my saxophone teacher -- I studied many times with different people and he was a beautiful musician and I remember one-- we were playing
